134	// ReadKubeletDynamicEnvFile reads the kubelet dynamic environment flags file a slice of strings.
135	func ReadKubeletDynamicEnvFile(kubeletEnvFilePath string) ([]string, error) {
136		data, err := os.ReadFile(kubeletEnvFilePath)
137		if err != nil {
138			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read file: %w", err)
139		}
140	
141		// Trim any surrounding whitespace.
142		content := strings.TrimSpace(string(data))
143	
144		// Check if the content starts with the expected kubelet environment variable prefix.
145		const prefix = constants.KubeletEnvFileVariableName + "="
146		if !strings.HasPrefix(content, prefix) {
147			return nil, errors.Errorf("the file %q does not contain the  expected prefix %q", kubeletEnvFilePath, prefix)
148		}
149	
150		// Trim the prefix and the surrounding double quotes.
151		flags := strings.TrimPrefix(content, prefix)
152		flags = strings.Trim(flags, `"`)
153	
154		// Split the flags string by whitespace to get individual arguments.
155		trimmedFlags := strings.Fields(flags)
156		if len(trimmedFlags) == 0 {
157			return nil, nil
158		}
159	
160		var updatedFlags []string
161		for i := 0; i < len(trimmedFlags); i++ {
162			flag := trimmedFlags[i]
163			if strings.Contains(flag, "=") {
164				// If the flag contains '=', add it directly.
165				updatedFlags = append(updatedFlags, flag)
166			} else if i+1 < len(trimmedFlags) {
167				// If no '=' is found, combine the flag with the next item as its value.
168				combinedFlag := flag + "=" + trimmedFlags[i+1]
169				updatedFlags = append(updatedFlags, combinedFlag)
170				// Skip the next item as it has been used as the value.
171				i++
172			}
173		}
174	
175		return updatedFlags, nil
176	}

Here's what I found about the kubeadm `NodeLocalCRISocket` feature and how it changes CRI socket handling via `instance-config.yaml`:

## The NodeLocalCRISocket Feature Gate

This feature (tracked as KEP-4656) changes how kubeadm stores and reads the container runtime interface (CRI) socket for each node. It adds a kubelet-instance-config file locally to store CRI sockets, and in kubeadm init, join and upgrade, overrides the global kubelet configuration through it.

### Core behavior change

With this feature gate enabled, kubeadm reads/writes the CRI socket for each node from/to the file /var/lib/kubelet/instance-config.yaml instead of reading/writing it from/to the annotation kubeadm.alpha.kubernetes.io/cri-socket on the Node object.

The new file is applied as an instance configuration patch, before any other user managed patches are applied when the --patches flag is used. It contains a single field containerRuntimeEndpoint from the KubeletConfiguration file format.

### How the value is applied

On each node, kubeadm detects the CRI socket and stores its details into the /var/lib/kubelet/instance-config.yaml file. When executing the init, join, or upgrade subcommands, kubeadm patches the containerRuntimeEndpoint value from this instance configuration into /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml.

### Upgrade fallback behavior

If the feature gate is enabled during upgrade, but the file /var/lib/kubelet/instance-config.yaml does not exist yet, kubeadm will attempt to read the CRI socket value from the file /var/lib/kubelet/kubeadm-flags.env.

## Related PRs for removing legacy CRI socket sources

Two pull requests handle cleanup of the old mechanisms during upgrade:

**PR #129278 — removing the flag from kubeadm-flags.env:** If the NodeLocalCRISocket feature is enabled, the container-runtime-endpoint arg in the kubeadm-flags.env file should be removed during the upgrade process. Otherwise, the containerRuntimeEndpoint field in the instance-config.yaml file will not take effect. Specifically, if the `NodeLocalCRISocket` feature gate is enabled, it removes the flag `--container-runtime-endpoint` from the `/var/lib/kubelet/kubeadm-flags.env` file on `kubeadm upgrade`.

**PR #129279 — removing the annotation (AnnotateCRISocket cleanup):** If the NodeLocalCRISocket feature is enabled, the kubeadm.alpha.kubernetes.io/cri-socket annotation in the node object should be removed during the upgrade, and the containerRuntimeEndpoint field will instead be obtained from instance-config.yaml. In other words, if the `NodeLocalCRISocket` feature gate is enabled, kubeadm removes the `kubeadm.alpha.kubernetes.io/cri-socket` annotation from a given node on `kubeadm upgrade`.

One caveat noted in that PR relates to dry-run mode: for dryrun mode, the fake node doesn't respect the feature-gate NodeLocalCRISocket.

## Annotation deprecation timeline

Starting from v1.34, this annotation is deprecated, and kubeadm will no longer actively set and use it. The feature graduated to Beta, as reflected in the documentation updates.

## Manually setting the CRI socket

If you need to change the runtime, you can work with this file directly. The kubeadm tool stores the host's CRI socket in the /var/lib/kubelet/instance-config.yaml file on each node. You can create this file on the node, which allows setting the containerRuntimeEndpoint parameter, and you can set this parameter's value to the path of your chosen CRI socket (for example unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock). Note that new CRI socket paths must be prefixed with `unix://` ideally.

An example of the file's contents looks like this:
```
containerRuntimeEndpoint: "unix:///run/containerd/containerd.sock"
```
This matches the observed format, alongside a kubeadm-flags.env that no longer contains the container-runtime-endpoint flag (only args like --node-ip and --pod-infra-container-image remain).

This design centralizes the CRI socket configuration per-node in a dedicated file rather than relying on the Node annotation (previously set by kubeadm's `AnnotateCRISocket`/patchnode phase) or the kubelet flags env file, which resolves ambiguity when multiple sources could conflict.
